 JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed this claim petition against respondents U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act 1989 seeking compensation in respect of death of Smt.Muktha K. Murthy W/o late C.V.Murali, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioner is as under:
On 18.12.2023 at about 09.30 a.m the deceased Muktha K. Murthy was riding her Scooter bearing (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.660/2024 No.KA-09-JK-8508 on the extreme left side of the road near GRS Fantasy Park, Ring Road, RBI Road Junction, Mysore City at that time the driver of concrete mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-09-D-4982 drove his vehicle in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the scooter of the deceased.
Due to this the deceased fell down on the road after which the rear wheel of the lorry ran over her body, as a result she succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
The petitioner has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
The petitioner is the only daughter of the deceased.

Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 49 years and she was employed as a Government High School Teacher and drawing salary of Rs.80.000/-
p.m and she was looking after the welfare and maintenance of the family.

Due to sudden and untimely demise of deceased has caused great grief and sarrow to the petitioner's family, there is nobody to look after her daily day to day needs, she is undergoing mental agony and great financial inconvenience, she is finding difficulty to eakout her daily day to day life and was depending upon the deceased for all her basis needs of day to day life.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.660/2024 driving of the driver of the offending concrete mixer Lorry and in this regard the VV Puram Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the said offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent No.1 is the RC Owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said offending vehicle,
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.2,00,00,000/- to the petitioner with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed written statement.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and contended that the alleged accident caused due to negligence of the deceased Muktha K. Murthy who rode her Scooter in rash and negligent manner and herself dashed the said scooter to the respondent No.1 Lorry, hence there is negligence on the part of the deceased and admits that driver of the said lorry had valid driving licence and valid insurance and hence, pray for dismiss the Sankeerthana M vs Krc Group on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160533097/
2 petition against respondent No.1.
05.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denies that the concrete mixer Lorry (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.660/2024 bearing No.KA-09-D-4982 stood insured with them as on the date of accident and the said insured vehicle was not all involved in the accident and the driver of the alleged vehicle was no way related in the alleged accident as on the date of accident and further contended that the driver of said Lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and thereby, the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and the alleged accident was happened due to the self negligence of deceased rider of the Scooter and caused this accident and there is no negligence on the part of the concrete mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-09-D-4982 and it is submitted that the driver of Lorry was driving with all the precautions and care and was observing all the rules and regulations prescribed by law.
It appears that the deceased rider of the third party vehicle was riding the vehicle rashly and negligently and failed to abide the traffic rules, thus, is sole responsible for the accident.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition against this respondent with costs.
06. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues have been framed:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioner proves that she is the LRs/dependent of deceased Smt.Muktha K. Murthy W/o late C.V.Mural?

02. Whether petitioner proves that deceased Smt.Muktha K. Murthy W/o late C.V.Murali, was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 18.12.2023 at about 9.30 a.m,
near GRS Fantasy Park, Ring road, RBI Road Junction, Mysore City, due to rash and negligent driving of concrete mixer Lorry bearing registration No.KA-09-D-4982 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?

07. The petitioner in order to prove her case, she herself got examined as PW.1 and got examined one witness as PW.2 and through them got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17 and closed her side evidence.
The counsel for the respondent No.2 submits no evidence.

Despite sufficient opportunity,
the respondent No.1 did not lead evidence.
Hence, respondent No.1 evidence is taken as nil and closed their side evidence.

08. The counsels for the petitioner and Sankeerthana M vs Krc Group on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160533097/
3 respondents have argued on main matter and perused the records.

09. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 :
As per final order  for the following:-

REASONS 10. Issues No.1 and 2:- Since these two issues are interconnected to each other and in order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record, these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
11. The petitioner in order to prove her case, she herself is examined as PW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though, she has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.660/2024 the case of the petitioner and during the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel she denied to the suggestion that her mother while going on the scooter she herself skid and fall and came with contact with the wheel of the lorry and she has not wore helmet and died and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the offending lorry and accident is occurred due to her negligence.
12. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 17 documents as Ex.P.1 to 17 on her behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the VV Puram Traffic Police against driver of offending lorry for his rash and negligent driving and death of deceased.
Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Sketch.
Ex.P.4 is copy of IMV report which indicates involvement of offending lorry in the accident.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Inquest Panchanama of deceased Muktha K. Murthy.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Post mortem report of deceased Muktha K. Murthy wherein it is stated that death is due to multiple injuries sustained.

Ex.P.7 is copy of Charge sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of the offending lorry for his rash and negligent driving and caused accident and caused death of the deceased.
Ex.P.8 is (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.660/2024 the copy of Aadhaar card of petitioner.
Ex.P.9 is the copy of Aadhaar card of deceased Muktha K. Murthy.
Ex. P.12 is copy of Mahazar and Ex.P.17 is the copy of Service book of deceased Muktha K. Murthy.

13. On going through the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, it appears that she is the daughter and legal representative and dependent on the earnings of the deceased and it is also proved that the deceased Muktha K. Murthy was died in road traffic accident that occurred on 18.12.2023 at about 09.30 a.m, near GRS Fantasy Park, Ring Road, RBI Road Junction, Mysore Sankeerthana M vs Krc Group on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160533097/
4 City, due to rash and negligent act of driving of concrete mixer Lorry bearing No.KA-09-D-4982 by its driver.

sentences.text: Accordingly, these Issues No.1 & 2 are answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Muktha K. Murthy, who died in vehicular accident.

The petitioner in her evidence and pleadings has stated that as on the date of alleged accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 49 years and she was employed as a Government High School Teacher and drawing salary of Rs.80.000/- p.m (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.660/2024 and has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
Due to sudden and untimely demise of deceased, she lost her beloved mother and she was entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
15. It is the duty of the petitioner to prove age, avocation and income of the deceased.
The petitioner has not produced any birth certificate or SSLC marks card for the proof of age of the deceased.

However, she has produced Ex.P.9 Aadhaar card, Ex.P.11 Identity card, Ex.P.13 Driving licence and Ex.P.7 Service book, and in the said documents the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 20.08.1974 and the alleged accident occurred on 18.12.2023.
Therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 49 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as on the date of accident is 49 years.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 46 to 50 years is 13.
16.

sentences.text:
So far as avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, the petitioner has examined a witness who is the Head Mistress of Government High (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.660/2024 School,
Megalapura, Mysore, as PW.2, in whose school the deceased was working as a Music Teacher Grade II (High School), since from 09.07.2010.

sentences.text: During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel, nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the evidence of petitioner and PW.2 regarding avocation and income of the deceased.

The petitioner and PW.2 have produced Ex.P.10 and 16, Pay slip for the month of September, October and November 2023 of deceased Muktha K.
Murthy.
The said Pay slip issued by the Government of Karnataka, wherein her gross salary is Rs.75,230/- for the month of November 2023.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.75,230/- p.m and it is multiplied by 12.
17.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & others case, future prospects or additional income is required to be added to the monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was aged 49 years and was a permanent employee, 30% of the income towards future prospects to be added to the income of the deceased, which would result in the income to be (75,230 + 22,569) (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.660/2024 Rs.97,799/-.

Since the petitioner is only one dependent,
it is appropriate to deduct 50% of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses and then her monthly income would be (97,799 - 48,899) Rs.48,899/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.48,899/-.
As the deceased was aged 49 years, a multiplier of 13 would have to be applied.

Consequently the petitioners would Sankeerthana M vs Krc Group on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160533097/
5 be entitled for a sum of Rs.76,28,244/- (Rs.48,899 x 12 x 13) towards loss of dependency.

18. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case in respect to loss of estate and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.

19. The claimant being only daughter of the deceased, she is entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of love and affection and Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Considering the facts (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.660/2024 and circumstances of the case and noticing the number of dependents and 1/2 of the income taken into consideration towards the personal and living expenses of the deceased, this Tribunal has placed reliance on ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;
Sl

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
. No . Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Loss of Dependency (After 76,28,244-00 deducting  of the income towards personal and living expenses)
2. Loss of love and affection 40,000-00 3. Loss of estate 19,500-00 4.
Funeral expenses and 19,500-00 transportation of dead body Total 77,07,244-00 20.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.77,07,244/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding loss of future prospects) from the date of petition till its realization.
21 . Regarding liability:-

Though the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared and filed written statement and contest the matter, but despite sufficient opportunity, they have not lead any evidence to disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove their defence.

The respondent No.1 in its written statement has admitted that it is the owner of the offending lorry and driver had a valid driving licence and said vehicle had a valid insurance policy as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.2 Insurance Company has not specifically denied issuance of policy with respect to offending lorry.
As per the averments made in the petition the insurance policy of the offending vehicle is valid from 11.07.2023 to 10.07.2024 and the alleged accident was occurred on 18.12.2023.
Therefore, it appears that as on the date of accident the policy of the offending vehicle is valid and is in force.

The respondent No.2 has not Sankeerthana M vs Krc Group on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160533097/
6 placed any material or evidence to show that owner or driver of the offending lorry have violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of the offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.660/2024 the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending lorry shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.77,07,244/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding loss of future prospects) from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, this Issue is answered partly in the affirmative.
22. Issue No.4:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.77,07,244/- (Rupees Seventy seven lakhs seven thousand two hundred and forty four only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a (excluding loss of future prospects) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, the petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.660/2024 the award amount through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.77,07,244/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding loss of future prospects) from the date of petition till its realization.

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.77,07,244/- (Rupees Seventy seven lakhs seven thousand two hundred and forty four only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a (excluding loss of future prospects) from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, the petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of (SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.660/2024 the award amount through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
